projects.name: Zimbabwe Resilience Building Fund 2 - UNDP
projects.description: The overall objective of the programme is to build resilience capacities of vulnerable rural communities, by ensuring sustainable natural resources management for climate action, improving food and nutrition security, and lower the impact of natural disasters in at-risk communities in Zimbabwe. This will be achieved through layering, sequencing and integration of 1: Evidence generation and capacity built for key institutions, systems, and communities for policy and programming that promote community stewardship on sustainable natural resources management and livelihood options. 2: Improved natural resources management, utilization, and environmental protection to promote sustainable food systems within functioning ecosystems for sustainable resilience to multiple shocks. 3: Enhanced sustainable, diversified livelihoods options for rural inclusive economic growth for at-risk communities. 4: Strengthened climate and disaster risk governance for resilience (early warning, and early action -Crisis Modifier) to cushion and protect developmental gains for at-risk communities. The implementation methodology of ZRBF Phase 2 will be anchored on two main approaches the landscape approach and programmatic approach. The Landscape Approach, a holistic and integrated method for land, resource, and ecosystem management. This approach is particularly suited to the diverse ecological, social, and economic contexts of the two targeted landscapes. In addition to the landscape approach, the programme will adopt a Programmatic Approach to ensure that activities are layered, sequenced, and integrated with other resilience-building efforts in the landscapes and beyond. The programmatic approach will allow for the coordination of ZRBF Phase 2 activities with ongoing government programmes, other donors and ongoing initiatives in the geographical areas.  The above four components are interconnected and are going to be implemented in an integrated and complimentary manner using a multilayered and multisectoral approach that address context specific development challenges. Given that resilience is dynamic and context specific interventions will be risk informed and embed DRM as the foundation for building resilience. The implementation approach ensures transformative change, sustainability and greater impact.

projects.name: HIV prevention for AGYW supported by CIDCA
projects.description:
The project, “Addressing High HIV Prevalence among Adolescent Girls and Young Women (AGYW) in Key Provinces in Zimbabwe,” aims to reduce new HIV infections among AGYW by 10% in four high HIV-burden provinces—Matabeleland South, Matabeleland North, Midlands, and Mashonaland Central—over a 24-month implementation period (2026–2028). The project will address key drivers of HIV infection, including limited access to HIV and sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services, adolescent pregnancies, early and forced marriages, school dropout, and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). Major interventions include HIV self-testing and linkage to care, demand creation for HIV and SRH services, provision of sanitary packs, peer-led awareness campaigns, community mobilization, male engagement as agents of change, strengthening community-led responses, and advocacy with traditional, religious, and political leaders to address harmful social norms. 
The project will utilize the Sister-to-Sister (Sista2Sista) model to empower AGYW through peer mentorship, link them to integrated HIV, SRH, and GBV services, and support informed reproductive health decision-making. It will also apply the SASA! (Start, Awareness, Support and Action) model to mobilize communities and address the root causes of gender-based violence through social norm change and engagement across all levels of society. The primary target population comprises adolescent girls and young women aged 10–24 years, including in-school girls, out-of-school girls, young single women, and married young women. The project is expected to reach 863,250 direct beneficiaries, primarily women and adolescent girls, while an additional 863,256 people will benefit indirectly, bringing the total beneficiary population to 1,726,506 people

projects.name: Eighth Operational Phase of the GEF Small Grants Programme (Part 1) – SGP OP8-Part 1
projects.description:
SGP-OP8 builds on 30 years of successful experience in empowering local CSOs and CBOs in community driven initiatives that have enhanced wellbeing, increased awareness and resilience, and generated global environmental benefits. With economic development pressures intensifying in the developing world and the associated rising inequalities, local communities, particularly vulnerable and disadvantaged groups are becoming increasingly marginalized. The objective of Part 1 of SGP OP8 is to engage local CSOs/CBOs in landscape-seascape approaches across the 99 participating countries, providing them access to knowledge and information, capacitating them through learning-by-doing, skills development, and delivering technical and grant assistance for interventions that enhance socioeconomic conditions and generate global environmental benefits. In line with the GEF-8 SGP Implementation Arrangements Paper, core SGP resources are to be allocated equally among all eligible countries.
The proposed strategy, elaborated through four complementary outcomes, reflects the key features of GEF Small Grants Programme 2.0, including new approaches to support youth, women and Indigenous Peoples, linking up with complementary partnerships, cooperating with the two additional GEF agencies, and leveraging opportunities with other GEF programs. SGP-OP8 will facilitate opportunities for innovation and scaling up, catalyze multi-stakeholder alliances, and leverage dialogue platforms for greater impact.
An important comparative advantage of SGP is the focus on social inclusion and vulnerable groups, including women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, the elderly and youth. Expected results under OP8-Part 1 include 225,000 ha of land and ecosystems under restoration, 3,800,000 ha of landscapes under improved practices, 90,000 ha of marine protected areas under improved management, 270,000 ha of marine habitat under improved practices, and 500,000 direct beneficiaries, of whom 250,000 are women.

projects.name: UNESCO_Ecosystem Restoration and Community Development in Protected Areas Programme
projects.description: The Ecosystem Restoration and Community Development Programme supports Zimbabwe by strengthening conservation and sustainable development in the Chimanimani Biosphere Reserve, an area of exceptional biodiversity that faces increasing pressures from climate change, floods, landslides, small-scale mining, and ecosystem degradation. These challenges threaten both ecological integrity and the livelihoods of local communities that depend on natural resources. The programme aims to restore ecosystems, improve biodiversity conservation, and enhance community resilience while promoting sustainable economic opportunities. Key activities include participatory environmental diagnostics, strengthening governance and institutional capacity of the biosphere reserve, restoring degraded ecosystems through reforestation and assisted natural regeneration, and installing monitoring systems to improve environmental management. The project will also support community cooperatives, develop local value chains, and promote indigenous knowledge and sustainable practices. Through training and capacity-building for park authorities, NGOs, women and youth, the programme will improve conservation management and community participation. Expected results include improved ecosystem health, strengthened biosphere reserve governance, increased income-generating opportunities for local communities, and enhanced long-term sustainability of the Chimanimani Biosphere Reserve as a model site for integrated conservation and development.
